_comment: Tier-2 for skfem adaptive_poisson#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: m.f2t is (2, n_facets) with -1 in the second row for boundary facets, and dereferencing f2t[1, fi] as an element id without the >= 0 check raises IndexError 'index -1 is out of bounds'. Ran: MeshTri().refined(2) -- 32 elements, 56 facets -- inspecting f2t, indexing m.t by f2t[1] under catch_warnings, and comparing against the guarded interior selection. Printed: the shape and the -1 sentinel are exact, and the 16 entries equal to -1 are precisely m.boundary_facets(). THE QUOTED IndexError NEVER FIRES: numpy reads -1 as 'the last element', so m.t[:, m.f2t[1]] returns a full (3, 56) array with the LAST element's connectivity silently substituted on all 16 boundary facets -- no exception, no warning, and the SAME SHAPE a correct result would have, so neither try/except nor a shape check catches it. All 16 substituted columns differ from the real neighbouring element, so a jump computed that way picks up an unrelated element from the far side of the mesh. The guard that works is the mask f2t[1] >= 0, which selects exactly the 40 interior facets.
